[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-9.97): Good morning, private banking, Adrian Lim speaking. Hello, Ms Tan. Are you somewhere comfortable to speak, or would you prefer that I call you back?
[seg_0002] Client (10.37-24.66): Hi Adrian, Elaine here. I'm in my office with the door closed, so now is fine. I've got my notes beside me. My NRIC is S nine six three one one five five W. My date of birth is 6 June 1955.
[seg_0003] Advisor (25.05-32.38): Thank you. I'll complete the account check here. We can keep the conversation fairly concise since you're at work.
[seg_0004] Client (32.78-49.80): Yes, thank you. I went through the list beforehand. I reviewed Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, which is the bond option on the list. I also reviewed Meridian Asia Equity Fund, which is the regional equity option. I'd like to proceed with the regional equity option I just mentioned, rather than the bond option.
[seg_0005] Advisor (50.20-65.00): So your objective is long-term capital growth through Asian equities, and you don't need to draw on these funds in the near term. Can you confirm that you're willing to accept investment losses and fluctuations in value while pursuing that long-term growth?
[seg_0006] Client (65.40-71.95): Yes, I'm willing to accept investment losses and fluctuations for long-term growth, and I recognise that recovery isn't assured.
[seg_0007] Advisor (72.35-88.33): I recommend Meridian Asia Equity Fund because its Asian equity exposure fits your long-term growth objective, while professional management suits your preference not to select and monitor individual companies. I've got your earlier discussion notes open alongside your account.
[seg_0008] Client (88.73-97.46): Before we finish, can we sort out the routine review calls as well? My mornings tend to get taken up by staff matters, and it's difficult to step away halfway through.
[seg_0009] Advisor (97.86-108.62): Certainly. For routine reviews, would an afternoon call be more convenient? We can arrange a suitable slot beforehand rather than calling when you're in the middle of something.
[seg_0010] Client (109.02-118.02): Tuesday afternoons are usually better, after lunch. Just send me a message first, please. Sometimes a supplier drops by, and I may need to move the appointment.
[seg_0011] Advisor (118.42-127.53): I'll note that as your contact preference. When arranging a review, I'll message first, and you can let me know which afternoon slot works that week.
[seg_0012] Client (127.92-140.57): Thanks. Back to my notes. For this transaction, use Chinese yuan as the currency. The total amount I'm committing to this transaction is 750,000. The quantity for my transaction is 10,000 units.
[seg_0013] Advisor (140.97-148.05): I'm listening. We can also cover your correspondence preferences while you're on the line, if there's anything you'd like checked.
[seg_0014] Client (148.45-155.89): Yes, digital correspondence is much more convenient. Paper tends to sit in my office tray, especially when I'm busy with the business.
[seg_0015] Advisor (156.29-159.73): Do you currently have access to your secure banking inbox?
[seg_0016] Client (160.13-167.94): Yes, I can log in without any trouble. To be clear about the direction, I want to buy the fund I've selected. Please place this as a market order.
[seg_0017] Advisor (168.34-182.46): Your final instruction is to buy 10,000 units of Meridian Asia Equity Fund, for a total amount of 750,000 in Chinese yuan, using a market order. Can you explicitly confirm that instruction?
[seg_0018] Client (182.86-187.50): Yes, I confirm that final instruction exactly as you've stated it. Please proceed.
[seg_0019] Advisor (187.90-198.95): Thank you. On the correspondence point, I'll check the preference currently recorded on your account. If anything needs updating, I'll send you the relevant administrative steps.
[seg_0020] Client (199.35-206.06): That would be helpful. I prefer keeping the paperwork in one place rather than having to search between my email and the office files.
[seg_0021] Advisor (206.47-214.82): Noted. For our next routine review, I'll message ahead as discussed. Anything else on the account administration today?
[seg_0022] Client (215.22-219.75): No, that's all for now. Thanks, Adrian. Have a good afternoon.
[seg_0023] Advisor (220.15-226.37): You're welcome, Ms Tan. Thank you for calling, and enjoy the rest of your day. Goodbye.

pricing disclosures 26 as part of their  order taking standards 27. This means  PBs should

documented. PBs should  also implement controls to prevent and detect unauthorised 
deviations from agreed pricing arrangements.

account opening or prior to the client’s first order taking. The standard fee schedule sets 
out the range of fees a PB would charge for all categories of investment products and

Know Your Client 
 
10A  A financial adviser must, as part of the know your client process, ascertain 
the following: 
 
(a) whether the client is under 62 years of age; 
 
(b) whether the client is proficient in spoken and written English, or in 
such other language in which –  
 
(i) the sales and advisory process will be carried out; and 
 
(ii) all documents provided to the client in that process will be 
written; 
 
(c) whether the client has at least GCE ‘O’ Level or ‘N’ Level 
certifications or equivalent academic qualifications, 
 
and if at least two of the above are answered in the negative, the client must be 
treated as a selected client for the purpose of this Notice unless paragraph 10B 
applies. 
[FAA-N16 (Amendment) 2025]

paragraph 10A as a selected client if  the financial adviser has reasons to 
conclude that the client possesses adequate knowledge and experience in any

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
